idea-plugin.name: AgentHub
idea-plugin.description:
AgentHub adds a toolbar button to every JetBrains IDE that launches any popular CLI coding agent in its own IDE terminal tab. Works with IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider and the rest.

Highlights

  • 40+ built-in agents — Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex CLI (OpenAI), Grok Build (xAI), Antigravity CLI (Google), Copilot CLI (GitHub), Cursor, Aider, Qodo, Qwen Code, Goose, OpenCode and many more.
  • Launch from the toolbar — or install a missing agent after a confirmation dialog.
  • Detection of installed agents on startup.
  • Project discovery — browse the projects and sessions of Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Freebuff, Grok Build, Junie CLI, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Kiro CLI, MiMo Code, Mistral Vibe, Oh My Pi, OpenCode and Qwen Code, and resume a session from the tool window.
  • Environment — see the skills, MCP servers, instruction files and configuration files each of those agents uses.
  • Shared skills — share a skill between agents, with a preview, backups and Undo.
  • Update notifications — a background check flags agents that have a newer version.
  • Manage from Settings — install, update or remove agents.
  • Custom agent — add your own CLI tool with a name, command and URL.
  • Companion tools — optional CLI utilities that work alongside the agents (usage tracking, context packing, skills); off by default.
  • Cross-platform — macOS, Linux and Windows (PowerShell helper script).
  • WSL mode (Windows) — optionally run every agent inside a WSL distribution instead of natively.

Open Settings/Preferences → Tools → AgentHub to choose which agents appear in the toolbar dropdown and to configure your custom agent.

Projects, Environment and Skills

The AgentHub tool window (right side of the IDE) shows the projects your coding agents have worked on, and the skills, MCP servers, instruction files and configuration files they use. Everything is read from local files and nothing is uploaded. Discovery is read-only. Skill files change only after you review a plan and confirm it.

  • Projects and Agents — sessions from Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Freebuff, Grok Build, Junie CLI, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Kiro CLI, MiMo Code, Mistral Vibe, Oh My Pi, OpenCode and Qwen Code, grouped by project or by agent. Sessions from several agents in the same repository appear as one project.
  • Sessions — each session shows the agent's title (or your first prompt), how many prompts you sent and when it ran. Resume reopens a session of any of these agents in its own CLI in a terminal; Transcript opens the session file.
  • Environment — skills, MCP servers, instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, …) and configuration files per project or agent. Skills and MCP servers that exist under several agents are marked as identical or different. MCP secrets are never shown, only variable names.
  • Skills — share a skill between agents, resolve conflicts, restore backups and undo. Every change shows a plan first and backs up what it replaces.
  • Installed agents only — only agents whose CLI the latest detection found are shown, even before their first session.
  • Open in IDE and Launch — open a project in a detected JetBrains IDE, or start an agent with the project directory as its working directory.
  • Cached index — kept across IDE restarts and refreshed in the background.

Supported agents

  • Aider — Aider AI
  • Amp — Sourcegraph
  • Antigravity CLI — Google
  • Auggie — Augment
  • Claude Code — Anthropic
  • Cline — Cline
  • CodeBuddy — Tencent
  • Codex CLI — OpenAI
  • Cody CLI — Sourcegraph
  • Command Code — Command Code
  • Continue CLI — Continue
  • Copilot CLI — GitHub
  • Crush — Charm
  • Cursor CLI — Cursor
  • Devin — Cognition
  • Droid — Factory AI
  • ForgeCode — Antinomy
  • Freebuff — Codebuff
  • Goose CLI — Block
  • Grok Build — xAI
  • iFlow CLI — iFlow
  • Junie CLI — JetBrains
  • Kilo Code — Kilo
  • Kimi Code — Moonshot AI
  • Kiro CLI — Kiro
  • Kode — shareAI-lab
  • LeanCTL — LeanCTL
  • MiMo Code — Xiaomi
  • Mistral Vibe — Mistral AI
  • Muse Code — Meta
  • Oh My Pi — can1357
  • OpenClaw — OpenClaw
  • OpenCode — SST
  • OpenHands — All Hands
  • Pi — Mario Zechner
  • Qodo — Qodo
  • Qoder CLI — Qoder AI
  • Qwen Code — Alibaba
  • SWE-agent — SWE-agent
  • VT Code — vinhnx

Command Code, ForgeCode, LeanCTL and Muse Code are hidden on Windows (no native Windows build, or a launch command that collides with a built-in Windows command). CodeRabbit CLI (companion tool) is hidden on Windows for the same reason (Windows support not released yet).

Companion tools — optional CLI utilities that work alongside the agents (off by default):

  • ccusage — token & cost usage reports from local agent logs
  • Claude Code Router — route Claude Code requests to other providers/models
  • Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor — live, predictive token & cost dashboard
  • code2prompt — codebase to LLM prompt, with Handlebars templating
  • CodeGrab — interactive TUI repo-context packer with secret redaction
  • CodeRabbit CLI — AI code reviews in the terminal
  • LiteLLM — self-hosted multi-provider LLM gateway with cost tracking
  • Repomix — pack your repository into an AI-friendly file
  • Semgrep CLI — static analysis security scanner
  • Skills — install reusable agent skills
  • TokenTracker — local token & cost dashboard
  • Tokscale — TUI token & cost dashboard with contribution graph
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.2

  • WSL mode covers the tool window. Projects, sessions, skills, MCP servers, instruction files and configuration are read from the distribution's home directory. Resume and Launch start inside the distro, and skill sync works on the distro's skill folders.
  • Windows (native) and every WSL distribution keep their own settings: enabled agents and tools, detection results and update status. Check installed agents / Check installed tools ticks what the last detection found.
  • Skills: a Redundant links / copies section with Remove link / Remove copy on the Overview and the Agents tab. Remove copy also swaps an identical copy of an agent that cannot read the shared folder for a link. Clean up redundant copies… covers both.
  • An already shared skill no longer offers Move to Shared. Skill icons and the agent filter show the agents a folder belongs to; system skills are grouped by agent.
  • Plandex was removed. The links of Auggie, Cody CLI, Droid, Grok Build, Muse Code, OpenHands and Qodo were updated.

1.3.1

  • The tool window discovers seven more agents: Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Oh My Pi, Junie CLI, Mistral Vibe, Freebuff and MiMo Code (17 in total) — projects and sessions, Skills, MCP servers, instruction files and Config.
  • Resume now works for all 17 agents, using each CLI's own resume command. A session id that is not safe to pass to a command line is refused rather than quoted.
  • Skills: the sync engine was reorganised, and symlinked skill folders are now walked. Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Oh My Pi, Junie CLI, Mistral Vibe and MiMo Code are Share/Promote targets.
  • Discovery fixes: Claude AGENTS.md and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, OpenCode .opencode and OPENCODE_CONFIG(_DIR), Qwen .qwen/rules, and same-named Antigravity MCP servers are listed separately. An instruction file that an agent does not apply is still listed, with an info line saying why.
  • The Agents tab lists every installed agent, also before its first session: Projects and Sessions are greyed out until then, and Environment already shows the agent's global skills, MCP servers, instructions and configuration.
  • Fewer needless rescans: AgentHub's own saves no longer look like changes made by another IDE, unchanged results are not written again, and the Skills and Environment data is no longer re-read and re-scanned on every click in the tool window.

1.3.0

  • New Skills tab: browse global or project skills, search and filter them, and open or reveal their files.
  • Share skills between agents. Share… is one checklist: check an agent to share with it, uncheck it to stop. An agent-specific skill can be moved to the shared folder from the same button. Resync / Repair, Stop Sharing and conflict resolution (keep the shared version, the agent's version, or both) are included.
  • Every change shows a plan first and takes a backup before replacing anything. Undo and Restore Backup… still work after an IDE restart.
  • Migrate duplicates… and Clean up redundant copies… tidy identical copies in one reviewed batch.
  • Settings: preferred Link or Copy mode, backups, an option to review plans before applying them, and Manage existing skills (off by default), which lets Stop Sharing also remove links and identical copies AgentHub did not create.
  • Skill ownership, history, settings and backups are shared by all JetBrains IDEs in ~/.agenthub. Existing data is imported automatically.
  • The Environment tab also lists agent configuration files (Config), with warnings for approval-bypass or unrestricted sandbox modes. Credentials and raw file contents are never stored.
  • Projects, Agents and Skills share one layout. Sessions show the agent's title (or your first prompt), the prompt count and the time range, plus token, model, cost and tool statistics where the agent records them. Resume works for Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode; Transcript opens the session file.
  • The tool window shows only agents whose CLI was found by the latest detection. Detection now runs on every IDE start.
  • Also: many smaller UI, layout, keyboard and accessibility fixes in the tool window and Settings.

1.2.0

  • New AgentHub Projects tool window with read-only project and session metadata discovery for Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Kiro CLI, OpenCode and Qwen Code
  • Unified Projects and Agents views with search, per-agent session totals, last activity, normalized Git identity and a persistent cached index
  • Open a discovered project in a detected JetBrains IDE or launch a participating coding agent directly in the project's working directory
  • Inspect normalized Skills, MCP servers and instruction sources in the new read-only project and agent Environment tabs, with availability comparison, duplicate and conflict indicators for Antigravity, Claude, Cline, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Grok, Kiro, OpenCode and Qwen Code
  • MCP secrets and executable configuration are never rendered in the UI
  • Discovery runs outside the UI thread, isolates malformed provider records and is covered by a 10,000-session performance regression test

1.1.2

  • New agent: Oh My Pi (can1357) — coding-first fork of Pi with LSP/DAP integration, browser & desktop tools, subagents and 60+ providers
  • Fix: "Update all agents" ran every installed agent's update command regardless of whether a newer version was actually available — it now only updates agents flagged outdated by the last "Check for updates" run, matching the per-agent Update button in Settings
  • Fix (Windows): a failing version-check command (e.g. a missing runtime dependency) was silently reported as "up to date" instead of a warning, since the error text was mistaken for the version string

1.1.1

  • New agent: Muse Code (Meta) — terminal coding agent for multi-agent, repo-scale software engineering tasks (WSL-only on Windows)
  • New companion tool: Semgrep CLI — static analysis security scanner

1.1.0

  • New: WSL mode (Windows) — Settings → Behavior → "Run agents in:" lets you run every agent/companion tool inside a WSL distribution instead of natively. Detection is distro-native (ignores Windows binaries exposed through WSL interop), Linux/WSL-only agents (ForgeCode, LeanCTL, Plandex, Command Code) become available, and a missing pip/npm in the distro produces an install hint instead of failing silently
  • New agent: Pi (Mario Zechner) — minimalist terminal coding agent harness
  • New companion tools: Claude Code Router, Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor, code2prompt, CodeGrab, CodeRabbit CLI, LiteLLM and Tokscale

1.0.0 — first stable release

  • New Companion Tools section — optional CLI utilities that work alongside the agents: ccusage, Repomix, Skills and TokenTracker (off by default; enable in Settings)
  • New agents: CodeBuddy (Tencent), Command Code, Devin (Cognition), iFlow CLI, Junie CLI (JetBrains), Kode and OpenClaw

0.9.1

  • New agent: Freebuff (Codebuff) — the free, ad-supported terminal coding agent
  • Fixes: Toolbar install of a not-installed agent now honors the "Run operations in background" setting; a background-installed agent launches automatically once ready
  • Lowered minimum platform to JetBrains IDE 2024.1+ (build 241+)

0.9.0 — Initial release

  • 30 built-in CLI coding agents
  • One-click launch from toolbar; not-installed agents prompt to install with confirmation
  • Auto-detect on first install and after each plugin update
  • Background update availability check on IDE startup
  • Install / Update / Remove directly from Settings panel
  • Custom agent support: configure your own CLI tool with name, command and URL
  • Cross-platform: macOS, Linux, Windows (PowerShell helper script)

group.description: Launch CLI coding agents in an IDE terminal. Auto-detects installed agents.
